analysis: The only changed file is landing/package-lock.json, a lockfile for the marketing/landing site. The patch bumps next 16.2.6 to 16.4.1, with matching @next/env, @next/swc-*, nested postcss 8.4.31 to 8.5.23, @swc/helpers, and sharp 0.34.5 to 0.35.5 with libvips 1.3.4. It also bumps fast-uri 3.1.8 to 3.1.9, undici 7.30.0 to 7.30.1 and source-map-js 1.2.1 to 1.2.2. The root dependency at head line 11 pins next to 16.4.1, consistent with the resolved entries. Changes are registry.npmjs.org URLs with new integrity hashes, and no non-registry or git sources are visible in the patch. sharp's `hasInstallScript` flag is removed, which reduces install-time script execution. sharp's node engine floor rises to >=20.9.0, matching next's existing >=20.9.0 requirement. A new optional sharp dependency on @img/sharp-freebsd-wasm32 and @img/sharp-webcontainers-wasm32 is added. The patch and range map suggest new lock entries (head lines ~1599-1662), but the head text for those entries is not supplied, so I could not verify their integrity hashes or sources. Nothing in the diff touches provider, coordinator, attestation, App Attest, key custody, or cache code. The threat model's assets (A-001 to A-018) and boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009 to TB-012) are not touched by this change, and no provider, native-runtime or release artifact path is affected. I identified no security regression. The residual uncertainty is limited to the unseen new lockfile entries and to whether the landing site shares any build pipeline with signed provider artifacts, which is outside the supplied evidence.
